entries.title: Have you bought a Kobo e-reader from Best Buy?
entries.summary: Who needs to touch grass? Experience Kobo IRL in over 500 Best Buy retail locations across the United States. The post Have you bought a Kobo e-reader from Best Buy? first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Rakuten Kobo began selling its e-readers at Best Buy retail stores and online in the United States. This began in August 2026, and we were the first to break the story. Customers have found that visiting a store and trying demo units helps them decide whether the device is right for them. Have you purchased a Kobo from Best Buy yet?

Book lovers across the United States can visit their local Best Buy to experience Kobo’s immersive reading technology firsthand. Customers can now browse, touch and purchase a range of Kobo products, including the compact, waterproof Kobo Clara Colour and Kobo Clara BW, the feature-rich, versatile Kobo Libra Colour and Kobo’s best-in-class accessories, such as Kobo Stylus 2 and Kobo Remote.

“Many readers want to be able to pick up a device, see the screen, and feel it in their hands before they commit. With Kobo eReaders now available at Best Buy, more American customers can do just that,” said Michael Tamblyn, CEO, Rakuten Kobo. “But the real magic happens once they get it home. We’ve built our e-readers to be an open, distraction-free space where the reader is in control. Whether that means endless reading with Kobo Plus, browsing our beautiful bookstore, seamless library borrowing with Libby, choosing a device with physical page-turn buttons, or simply enjoying an ad-free experience, we’re focused on making sure Kobo devices work exactly the way you want them to. We’re excited to make it easier for every kind of reader to find that right fit—an avid reader who wants to carry their entire library wherever they go, or someone looking for a more affordable, convenient way to get lost in a story.”

This retail expansion reinforces Kobo’s commitment to growing its footprint and supporting the global reading community. Whether you are a dedicated bookworm or looking for the perfect gift for a reader, the latest Kobo eReaders are now ready for pickup at a Best Buy near you.

For more information on Kobo e-readers or to find a participating Best Buy location, visit here.

entries.title: What is the Audible BOGO Sale?
entries.summary: Audible runs BOGO sales every few months. What is a BOGO sale? How does it work? What do you need to do to get audiobook discounts? The post What is the Audible BOGO Sale? first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Audible audiobooks are digital voice recordings of books that you listen to instead of reading, provided by Audible, the world’s largest producer and retailer of audiobooks and spoken-word entertainment. Owned by Amazon, the service allows you to stream or download audiobooks, podcasts, and exclusive audio content directly to your smartphone, tablet, computer, or Amazon Echo device.

Every couple of months, Audible has a BOGO sale for audiobooks. What is a BOGO sale? An Audible BOGO sale (often called the 2-for-1 Credit Sale) is a recurring, member-only promotion that lets you buy two audiobooks for the price of one credit. Instead of spending one credit per book, your single membership credit covers both titles.

To participate, you must be an active subscriber to an Audible Premium Plus or Premium plan and have at least one available credit in your account. The sale does not apply to the entire Audible store. Instead, Audible curates a specific promotional page featuring hundreds of eligible books across various genres.

You must select two books from the designated sale list. When you add the first title to your promotional cart, the system will prompt you to add a second. Once both are in your cart, you check out using a single credit. Just like regular credit purchases, any books you buy during a BOGO sale belong to you forever, even if you eventually cancel your membership.

You can view the various BOGO sales on the Audible BOGO page. You can bookmark it, and it updates regularly with new titles every couple of months.

entries.title: CloudLibrary is coming to Kobo e-Readers
entries.summary: Rakuten Kobo is running a trial period for select Canadian and US libraries using CloudLibrary with Send to Kobo. The post CloudLibrary is coming to Kobo e-Readers first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
CloudLibrary is a platform libraries use to manage their e-book and audiobook collections, similar to Overdrive Libby. CloudLibrary and Kobo appear to be working on an integration that is undergoing a trial period with select libraries in September, with a broader rollout to the Kobo Clara Color, Kobo Clara BW, and Kobo Libra Color in October.

In the CloudLibrary app or on the website, click Send to Kobo next to a title to borrow it and send it to your Kobo eReader. You can also borrow CloudLibrary books from various libraries’ online catalogs. But the ‘Send to Kobo’ button is only available in the CloudLibrary app or on the website, so you will need to go there to send anything to your Kobo. The trial also works only with e-books, not audiobooks.

It remains to be seen if Kobo will include a CloudLibrary system similar to Libby, where you can browse your local branch’s online catalog right on the e-reader and attach your card in the settings menu. It is unlikely that you will be able to attach more than one CloudLibrary account on the Kobo e-reader.

Here are some tips about the beta

  • The borrowed book will be removed from the Kobo upon its expiry date.
  • If a book is renewed in the CloudLibrary app or website it must be sent to the Kobo again.
  • If you read the book on the CloudLibrary app or website in addition to reading it on the Kobo, your reading position will not be synchronized with the Kobo.
  • A CloudLibrary account can only be connected to one Kobo account.

entries.title: Tapmora E INK Fridge Magnet Review
entries.summary: Whether it’s a goofy snapshot of your pet, a breathtaking view from your last road trip, or a daily motivational quote to start your morning—Tapmora makes your space uniquely yours. The post Tapmora E INK Fridge Magnet Review first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Tapmora is an electronics brand best known for creating the world’s first battery-free E Ink Photo Magnet. The device is a cordless, pocket-sized digital frame that lets users instantly transfer smartphone photos to a paper-like, magnetic display without charging cables, Wi-Fi, or Bluetooth. It retails for $45 and is available to order from the company’s website.

The Tapmora E Ink Photo Magnet offers a clever, low-maintenance way to display digital memories without the clutter of charging cables. Its standout feature is NFC energy harvesting, letting users push photos directly from a smartphone app with a simple tap. Reviewers note that using the Spectra 6 full-color array pays off significantly; unlike cheaper 4-color portable panels that turn vibrant landscapes or skin tones into muddy grays, Tapmora preserves color accuracy and rich tones. The passive, matte, paper-like display blends smoothly into refrigerators or desks, offering a premium “printed” aesthetic that feels much more organic than a harsh, glowing LCD screen.

However, the tech comes with clear trade-offs, depending on your expectations. Because the screen relies entirely on a temporary burst of electricity harvested from your phone’s NFC chip, image transfers take a few seconds, and the device lacks backlighting or built-in buttons for manual refreshes. While it aligns with the industry’s shift toward pocket-sized magnetic smart tiles, it operates strictly as a static canvas rather than a responsive gadget. Ultimately, it is a beautifully packaged niche novelty that offers great value for anyone looking to ditch instant film or static prints, though it may not fully satisfy tech enthusiasts seeking interactive functionality.

entries.title: Onyx Boox Note Air 6C Now Available on Amazon
entries.summary: The latest-generation Boox Note Air 6C is now available to order on Amazon.com in the United States and will start shipping on September 22nd. The post Onyx Boox Note Air 6C Now Available on Amazon first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Onyx Boox announced its latest-generation Note Air 6C a couple of days ago, and it is already available to order on Amazon. This tablet features a 10.3-inch color E Ink display and serves as a high-performance productivity tablet built to run full workflows with paper-like visual comfort.

The display features a next-generation Kaleido 3 color screen protected by an anti-glare flat cover-lens and illuminated by a dual-tone adjustable front light. It delivers crisp 300 ppi clarity for black-and-white content and 150 ppi for 4,096 vibrant colors. BOOX Super Refresh (BSR) technology drives page transitions and scrolling, increasing page-turn speeds by 40% to 45% and significantly reducing visual ghosting compared to previous models. It features a 10.3-inch color E Ink display, an upgraded 4nm octa-core processor, 6GB RAM, and 64GB of internal storage (expandable up to 2TB via microSD). Running Android 16 with full Google Play Store access, it features a tablet-style UI complete with customizable widgets and a dedicated app dock.

This tablet is now confirmed to use WACOM instead of the BOOX EMR, with the Inksense stylus they use on all their other e-notebooks these days. I suppose that is what happens when BOOX recycles the same industrial design for multiple generations.

BOOX Tablet 10.3" Note Air6 C 6GB 64GB E Ink Tablet Color ePaper Notebook

  • Screen: 10.3" Kaleido 3 (4,096 colors) glass screen with flat cover-lens. Resolution: B/W: 2480 x 1860 (300 ppi). Color: 1240 x 930 (150 ppi). Touch: BOOX stylus with magnetic type + capacitive touch. CPU: Qualcomm 6690 + BSR GPU. RAM: 6GB. ROM: 64GB. Connectivity: Wi-Fi + BT 6.0. Front Light with CTM (Warm and Cold)
  • OS: Android 16. Document Formats: PDF, CAJ, DJVU, CBR, CBZ, EPUB, EPUB3, AZW3, MOBI, TXT, DOC, DOCX, FB2, CHM, RTF, HTML, ZIP, PRC, PPT, PPTX. Image Formats: PNG, JPG, BMP, TIFF, GIF. Audio Formats: WAV, MP3 Supports 3rd-party apps
  • Button: Power Button with Fingerprint Recognition USB-C Port (Supports OTG or use as an audio jack) microSD Card Slot Built-in Dual Speakers Built-in Microphone. Battery: 3,700mAh Li-ion Polymer. Battery Dimensions: 225 x 192 x 5.8 mm (8.9" x 7.6" x 0.23") Weight: Approx. 440 g (15.5 oz)

entries.title: XTEINK X4 Classic and X4 Pro Now Available on Amazon
entries.summary: XTEINK X4 Classic and XTEINK X4 Pro are now available to order from Amazon.com in the United States. The post XTEINK X4 Classic and X4 Pro Now Available on Amazon first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The XTEINK X4 Classic and X4 Pro are now available to order on Amazon.com in the United States. This lets customers get fast shipping on their e-readers and return them within the standard return window. Ordering directly from the XTEINK website can take weeks to arrive.

The XTEINK X4 Classic features a compact 4.3-inch E Ink display housed in an ultra-thin body that weighs approximately 68 grams. Sticking to a distraction-free physical layout, it omits both a touchscreen and a front light, opting instead for front and side buttons for all navigation, as highlighted in a detailed review. The device also includes a magnetic backplate for easy integration with everyday carry. Under the hood, an upgraded ESP32-S3 processor and a 920 mAh battery deliver longer battery life. For storage, it comes with 16 GB of internal capacity, expandable via a microSD card slot, and supports standard reading formats such as EPUB, TXT, MOBI, and PDF. Wireless connectivity features include built-in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. The XTEINK X4 Classic has pogo pins and uses a magnetic pogo-pin connection instead of a standard USB-C port.

The X4 Pro features a 4.3-inch E-Ink touchscreen with a resolution of 220 PPI. The lighting system is the most anticipated upgrade. It lets you read comfortably in the dark or in low-light environments without a separate clip-on reading lamp. Despite adding layers for the light and touch sensors, the Pro model measures an incredibly slim 5.98mm, making it slightly thinner than the original X4’s 6.4mm. It retains its physical page-turn buttons alongside the new touchscreen, giving you tactile control when flipping pages.

It has 16 GB of fixed internal memory for reading e-books, plus an SD card slot that supports up to 256GB. It has a paltry 8MB of RAM, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth. It is powered by a 1100mAh battery, which should last a month of reading. Unlike the standard USB-C on the first-generation X4, the X4 Pro uses a magnetic, bespoke pogo-pin charging cable.

XTEINK X4 Classic Pocket eReader, Ultra-Light 68g & 4.9mm Thin, Space Black

  • Paper-Feel E-Ink Display & Focused Reading: Enjoy focused reading on a 4.3" E-Ink display with a paper-feel viewing experience. The glare-free screen and distraction-free system keep notifications and ads away, helping you stay immersed in your books.

XTEINK X4 Pro 4.3" ebook Reader with Front Light & Touchscreen, Space Black

  • Ultra-Compact, Magnetic & Portable: Exceptionally compact with a 5.95mm ultra-thin profile and 72g (2.5 oz) lightweight design. Fits effortlessly into any pocket or palm, featuring a built-in magnetic back for seamless attachment and portable carry anywhere.
  • Eye-Care E-Ink with Dual-Tone Front Light: Premium 4.3" paper-feel display that eliminates screen glare and eye fatigue. Equipped with multi-level warm and cool front light controls for a comfortable reading experience in bright sunlight or complete darkness.
  • Touchscreen & Physical Page-Turn Buttons: Features intuitive single-point touch and gesture swiping combined with tactile side page-turn buttons. Offers dual control options for fluid, precise, and effort-free page navigation.

entries.title: Kobo changes its ebook Price Match System
entries.summary: Rakuten Kobo has changed its Price Match Guarantee and will no longer provide an extra 10% savings. The post Kobo changes its ebook Price Match System first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Rakuten Kobo offers a Price Match Guarantee for eBooks and audiobooks, allowing you to receive store credit for the price difference if you find the same digital title cheaper elsewhere. The service launched in 2016, but Kobo does not price-match hardware like e-readers or accessories.

Kobo has just changed the terms of its Price Match system. Previously, you would receive the price difference plus an additional 10% discount. The company has been emailing customers and was told the following: “We would like to inform you that we have updated our Price Match Guarantee policy. The update removes the additional 10% discount previously offered on top of the competitor’s price. Going forward, our Price Match Guarantee will only match the verified competitor’s price.

One downside of the change is that Kobo’s credits don’t account for sales tax paid on the higher of the two prices. The 10% helped to close that gap.

entries.title: Ugreen annouces Spectra E INK Case for iPhone 18 Pro
entries.summary: UGREEN's Magic E-ink Screen Case is a new protective accessory for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max that adds a color E-Ink display to the back of the phone The post Ugreen annouces Spectra E INK Case for iPhone 18 Pro first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The UGREEN Magic E-ink Screen Case for the iPhone 18 Pro integrates a six-color e-ink display on the back, offering a budget-friendly, creative canvas for personalization. While it offers traditional drop protection features and syncs custom images via a companion app, the panel is strictly static and lacks interactive functions, video playback, or global pricing details.

You get a full-color E Ink display, as the name suggests, that you can use to show photos stored on your iPhone. You sync the case to the device, then send digital images to the extra screen. It was announced on Ugreen’s Weibo feed alongside several other iPhone accessories. It is also unknown if the accessory will launch outside China.

I think this device uses a Spectra Panel, since the product uses six colors; it must use the E Ink Spectra 6 display, which features six primary base colors: black, white, red, yellow, blue, and green.

entries.title: TICKEY is a new e-paper badge now on Crowdfunding
entries.summary: The ENILINX TICKEY is a pocket-sized, 3.7-inch color e-Paper smart badge and digital desk display. The post TICKEY is a new e-paper badge now on Crowdfunding first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The ENILINX TICKEY is a highly versatile, pocket-sized 3.7-inch color e-Paper smart badge and desk display. Launched through a highly successful Kickstarter campaign that raised over $900,000, it’s a premium, non-disposable accessory that serves multiple roles, including an event badge, bag charm, desk display, or digital fridge note.

The ENILINX TICKEY is a pocket-sized smart badge with a 3.7-inch color e-Paper screen that renders 48+ native colors and uses zero power to maintain static images. Encased in a slim, ultra-thin anodized aluminum body with customizable front frames, the hardware includes a versatile mounting array with a clip ring, built-in magnetic back, and integrated desk stand. It delivers exceptional power efficiency, letting its rechargeable battery last up to two months on a single charge under daily use.

Under the hood, the device runs on an Espressif ESP32-S3 microcontroller, making it fully open-source and highly programmable for custom firmware development. It features robust wireless connectivity with Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and NFC integration, enabling seamless smartphone customization via companion apps alongside instant digital business card or URL sharing. These specifications allow the badge to dynamically shift roles between a wearable event accessory, an automated desk display, a system monitoring dashboard, or an interactive smart home node.

entries.title: The Onyx Boox Picco is running Crosspoint
entries.summary: The Boox Picco runs on a custom fork of CrossPoint; it is not an official CrossPoint release. Onyx has also confirmed that the Piccoo runs on the ESP32 platform. The post The Onyx Boox Picco is running Crosspoint first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
There has been some conjecture on what type of operating system the Onyx Boox Picco is employing. Onyx is cagey about it right now, but a website that received the firmware says it’s running a custom fork of CrossPoint; it is not an official CrossPoint release. Onyx has also confirmed that the Piccoo runs on the ESP32 platform and that this system is responsive, easy to navigate, and packed with rich reading features that meet lightweight usage needs.

Onyx Boox has quietly said that “we are aware that products with similar hardware configurations on the market support installing third-party firmware. However, we do not recommend attempting this. Modifying the firmware or flashing third-party firmware may not only damage your device, but also void its warranty.” This comment likely comes from customers asking whether they can install the official CrossPoint release for more functionality.

The Picco features a 3.97″ Monochrome Screen with a resolution of 480 x 800 and 235 PPI. It has both warm and cool lighting that you can switch with a button. Under the hood is an unknown processor, with a 16 GB Card Included, which is expandable to 2 TB. All data and e-books are stored on the card. The BOOX Picco features a USB-C port that supports charging. You can charge the device with a USB-C cable. You will transfer e-books and pictures with the BOOX Tiles app or the web. It has Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, runs on a 920 mAh battery, and measures 105.5 x 62 x 5.5 mm; it weighs 58 g.

The Picco supports EPUB, MOBI, AZW3, AZW, AZW5, FB2, FB2.ZIP, FB3, FBZ, TXT, PDB, PRC, RTF, HTML, XHTML, HTM, and CHM ebook formats. It includes a few apps, such as Pomodoro, Todo, and Countdown.

The Picco retails for $99, and you can read more and order one HERE.
